title: macOS: Updating Tailscale forces re-login and creates a new device entry instead of reusing existing one
body:
### What is the issue?

After every Tailscale update on macOS, the app requires a new login. Once logged in again, a new device appears in the Tailscale admin panel instead of reusing the previous device identity.

This creates confusion and clutter, since each update effectively registers the same physical Mac as a new device each time.

comments.author: participant13
comments.body:
I was having the same issue and came across this thread in the support forums. I appreciate the troubleshooting completed so far. I imagine turning off automatic updates till it is fixed will be the best method going forward till the bug is resolved.

For those looking to the 1.88.2 package for a downgrade, it is here: https://<redacted-host>/stable/?v=1.88.2

Do a complete uninstall following these instructions: https://tailscale.com/kb/1069/uninstall?tab=macos+%28standalone%29

To make for quick cleanup use this bash script: 

```
#!/bin/bash

echo "Removing Tailscale leftovers…"

# Expand ~ safely
USER_HOME="${HOME}"

# Paths to remove
paths=(
    "$USER_HOME/Library/Application Scripts/*.io.tailscale.ipn.macsys"
    "$USER_HOME/Library/Application Scripts/io.tailscale.ipn.macsys"
    "$USER_HOME/Library/Application Scripts/io.tailscale.ipn.macsys.login-item-helper"
    "$USER_HOME/Library/Application Scripts/io.tailscale.ipn.macsys.share-extension"
    "$USER_HOME/Library/Caches/io.tailscale.ipn.macsys"
    "$USER_HOME/Library/Containers/io.tailscale.ipn.macsys"
    "$USER_HOME/Library/Containers/io.tailscale.ipn.macsys.login-item-helper"
    "$USER_HOME/Library/Containers/io.tailscale.ipn.macsys.share-extension"
    "$USER_HOME/Library/Containers/Tailscale"
    "$USER_HOME/Library/Group Containers/*.io.tailscale.ipn.macsys"
    "$USER_HOME/Library/HTTPStorages/io.tailscale.ipn.macsys"
    "$USER_HOME/Library/Preferences/io.tailscale.ipn.macsys.plist"
    "/Library/Tailscale"
)

for path in "${paths[@]}"; do
    # Expand globs manually
    for target in $(echo $path); do
        if [ -e "$target" ]; then
            echo "→ Removing: $target"
            rm -rf "$target"
        else
            echo "→ Skipping (not found): $target"
        fi
    done
done

echo "Done! Tailscale remnants have been cleaned up." 
```

comments.author: participant21
comments.body:
Seeing the same issue on an Intel MacBook Pro running macOS 13.1 with Tailscale 1.98.5.

After updating Tailscale, it required re-authentication and registered the same physical Mac as a new machine with a new 100.x address, leaving the previous admin-console machine entry stale/dead. Disabling key expiry on the old machine didn't prevent this.

I then ran:

`defaults write ~/Library/Preferences/io.tailscale.ipn.macsys.plist EncryptState -bool false`
`killall cfprefsd`

Confirmed `EncryptState` reads `0`.

After that, the first re-auth still created one new machine entry, presumably because the previous local state was already lost. But after keeping the newest entry, quitting/restarting Tailscale and using “renew session” no longer created further duplicate machines.

So the workaround appears to prevent future duplicates on 1.98.5/macOS 13.1, but doesn't attach back to the already-existing stale machine entry once the local state has been lost.
